# RZ-SNARL qPCR Comparison: Model 0 (qPCR technical noise)

**Objective**: Model RZ qPCR well-to-well noise and per-well detection as a function of load, from eDNA extracts run in triplicate wells on one plate. Posterior draws and the noise and detection curves are exported for use in Model 2 (`rz_snarl_qpcr_model2_experiment.qmd`).

Experiment results are single wells, so per-well noise and detection are the relevant quantities. Wells of one extract on one plate share a standard curve, so this is **within-plate** noise only (pipetting, Poisson sampling of copies into the well, amplification). It is a lower bound on the qPCR noise between the experiment's shared-extract results, which were run on different plates in different labs.

## Setup

Load packages; load and clean eDNA data (`R/edna_prep.R`, from data saved by `R/edna_import.R`) and experiment data (`R/data_prep.R`, for comparing load ranges)

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Setup code"
#| results: hide
librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, knitr, kableExtra, ggplot2, patchwork, brms, cmdstanr, posterior, bayesplot)

cmdstanr::check_cmdstan_toolchain()   # confirms Stan is found
set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

source(here("R", "data_prep.R"))
source(here("R", "edna_prep.R"))

# fitted models are saved outside the repo
fit_dir = here(wddir, "fits")
dir.create(fit_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# set TRUE to refit models instead of loading saved fits
refit = FALSE

# include tissue extracts (higher loads, different matrix)
include_tissue = TRUE
# include samples with no detected well (mostly true absence in eDNA; see Model structure)
include_all_zero = FALSE

# latent load distribution of sample intercepts: "student" (df fixed at student_df) or "normal"
latent_dist = "student"
student_df = 4

# centre of the sigma load covariate (log10 Bd load per swab, Qiagen scale)
load_center = 2.5
```

## Model 0: qPCR technical noise

Per-well noise and detection as a function of load, as a brms hurdle-lognormal model (cmdstanr backend), following Model 1.

- **Latent load**: each sample (one extract, on its latest run) has a group-level intercept in `mu`, its true (log) load. By default (`latent_dist = "student"`), group-level intercepts are Student-t with degrees of freedom fixed at `student_df` (4), so the few high-load samples (tissue, some Sierra Nevada eDNA) sit at their own loads instead of being shrunk into the eDNA bulk just above the detection limit. Estimating the degrees of freedom did not converge (`df` ≈ 1.9, Rhat 1.10, 28 divergences): with ~3 wells per sample the tail shape is not identified, and the near-Cauchy fit had a very narrow core (scale ≈ 0.15 log10) that pulled samples with one detected well toward the centre, so the median positive load was overpredicted. `latent_dist = "normal"` is a sensitivity check, and shows that Student-t intercepts are required: with normal intercepts, the high-load samples are again shrunk (to ≈ 2.3–2.5 log10, including the three wells at 5.3 log10) and explained by a large `sigma`, so the `sigma` slope turns positive (+0.88 per log10) and replicated within-sample SD above 3 log10 is ≈ 1.5 (90% 0.7–3.4) vs. 0.05 observed; the `sigma` load covariate does not prevent this. With Student-t (df = 4), samples with three detected wells stay on the 1:1 line up to 5.3 log10. Remaining shrinkage is at the low end: single-well samples observed below ≈ 1.8 log10 (≈ 1.5 copies per reaction) are pulled up to ≈ 1.8, since their large `sigma` makes one well weakly informative.
- **Detection**: `hu` (probability a well is not detected) has a group-level intercept correlated with `mu`, so the `mu`–`hu` correlation gives the per-well detection curve.
- **Noise**: `sigma` (well-to-well SD) depends on `load_obs_c`, each sample's observed mean log10 load of its detected wells (centred at `load_center`), plus an independent sample-level intercept for extra between-sample variation. Log noise is linear in log load, which matches Poisson sampling at low copy numbers (SD ∝ 1/√copies) but has no floor at high loads. An observed covariate is used because a first version, with a `sigma` intercept correlated with `mu`, was degenerate: the narrow normal latent-load distribution shrank high-load samples (e.g. three wells at 5.3 log10 agreeing within 0.01) to ≈ 2.8 log10 and explained them with a huge `sigma`, giving a spurious positive load–noise correlation (+0.58) and a failed within-sample SD check. The covariate is noisy for samples with one detected well, but these carry no information on `sigma`.
- **Samples with no detected well are left out** by default (`include_all_zero = FALSE`). In eDNA most of them are true absences, not missed detections, and would pile up at the low end of the latent-load distribution. The cost is that detection at the lowest loads is overestimated (samples with low load that happened to give 0/3 wells are missing). Set `include_all_zero = TRUE` for a sensitivity check.

`mu` and `sigma` are on the natural-log scale of Bd load (ITS1 copies per swab, Qiagen scale: 40 × copies per reaction); results are converted to log10 for plots, on both scales.

### Model data

```{r m0-data}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Model data code"

m0_df = edna_clean %>%
  filter(include_tissue | !is_tissue) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  filter(include_all_zero | any(detected)) %>%
  mutate(load_obs = if_else(any(detected), mean(log10(bd_load[detected])), NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sample_type = if_else(is_tissue, "tissue", "eDNA"),
         # samples with no detected well (include_all_zero) get the centre; sigma does not enter their likelihood
         load_obs_c = coalesce(load_obs - load_center, 0))

m0_df %>%
  group_by(sample_type) %>%
  summarise(samples = n_distinct(sample),
            plates = n_distinct(plate),
            wells = n(),
            detected = mean(detected),
            samples_2plus_detected = n_distinct(sample[detected][duplicated(sample[detected])]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Model structure

```{r m0-structure}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Model structure code"

m0_family = hurdle_lognormal()

# sample intercepts, shared (correlated) between mu and hu
# (brms calls the normal "gaussian")
m0_group = sprintf('(1 | g | gr(sample, dist = "%s"))', if (latent_dist == "normal") "gaussian" else latent_dist)

m0_formula = bf(
  as.formula(paste("bd_load ~ 1 +", m0_group)),

  as.formula(paste("hu ~ 1 +", m0_group)),

  sigma ~ 1 + load_obs_c +
    (1 | sample)
)

m0_priors = c(
  # mu (ln copies per swab; eDNA positives are mostly 1-30 copies per reaction, i.e. ~40-1200 per swab)
  prior(normal(5, 3), class = "Intercept"),

  # hu
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept", dpar = "hu"),

  # sigma (log of ln-scale SD; -1 ~ 0.16 log10); slope per log10 load (Poisson: -0.5 * ln(10) ~ -1.15)
  prior(normal(-1, 1), class = "Intercept", dpar = "sigma"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b", dpar = "sigma"),

  # group-level effects (sd priors are set per dpar; class = "sd" alone covers mu only)
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "sigma"),
  prior(lkj(2), class = "cor")
)

# Student-t degrees of freedom fixed (not identified with ~3 wells per sample)
if (latent_dist == "student") {
  m0_priors = m0_priors +
    set_prior(sprintf("constant(%s)", student_df), class = "df", group = "sample")
}
```

### Fit

Fit is saved to `fits/` in the data directory (`m0_qpcr_noise_student.rds` or `m0_qpcr_noise_normal.rds`, by `latent_dist`) and reloaded unless `refit = TRUE`.

```{r m0-fit}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Fit code"
#| results: hide

m0 = brm(
  formula = m0_formula,
  data = m0_df,
  family = m0_family,
  prior = m0_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 1234,
  cores = 4,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  file = here(fit_dir, paste0("m0_qpcr_noise_", latent_dist)),
  file_refit = if (refit) "always" else "on_change"
)
```

### Convergence & summary

```{r m0-summary}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Summary code"

summary(m0)

# group-level correlation: mu-hu (detection vs load)
posterior_summary(m0, variable = "^cor_sample", regex = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Noise and detection curves

Population-level curves. **Detection**: for a sample with latent log load `mu`, the conditional distribution of its `hu` intercept (bivariate Student-t with `mu`; normal if `latent_dist = "normal"`, where the scale factor below is 1) has mean shifted by $\rho \, sd_{hu} / sd_\mu \, (\mu - \mu_0)$ and scale $sd_{hu}^2 (1 - \rho^2) (\nu + z^2) / (\nu + 1)$, with $z = (\mu - \mu_0) / sd_\mu$; detection averages over this spread (probit approximation to the logistic-normal, as in Model 1, treating the conditional t as normal). **Noise**: median well-to-well SD across samples at a given load, $\exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 (\text{log10 load} - \text{load\_center}))$, converted to log10.

```{r m0-curves-calc}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show curve calculation code"

m0_pop = as_draws_df(m0) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  transmute(draw = .draw,
            mu_0 = b_Intercept,
            hu_0 = b_hu_Intercept,
            sigma_0 = b_sigma_Intercept,
            sigma_slope = b_sigma_load_obs_c,
            sd_mu = sd_sample__Intercept,
            sd_hu = sd_sample__hu_Intercept,
            rho_hu = cor_sample__Intercept__hu_Intercept,
            # fixed df; Inf = normal intercepts
            nu = if (latent_dist == "student") student_df else Inf)

m0_curve_draws = expand_grid(m0_pop, log10_load = seq(1, 5, by = 0.05)) %>%
  mutate(mu = log10_load * log(10),
         z = (mu - mu_0) / sd_mu,
         hu_mean = hu_0 + rho_hu * sd_hu * z,
         # conditional t scale factor (nu + z^2) / (nu + 1); 1 for normal intercepts
         hu_var = sd_hu^2 * (1 - rho_hu^2) * if_else(is.infinite(nu), 1, (nu + z^2) / (nu + 1)),
         p_detect = 1 - plogis(hu_mean / sqrt(1 + pi * hu_var / 8)),
         # ln-scale SD -> SD of log10(load)
         sigma_log10 = exp(sigma_0 + sigma_slope * (log10_load - load_center)) / log(10))

m0_curves = m0_curve_draws %>%
  pivot_longer(c(p_detect, sigma_log10), names_to = "curve") %>%
  group_by(curve, log10_load) %>%
  summarise(med = median(value),
            lo = quantile(value, 0.05),
            hi = quantile(value, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(log10_copies = log10_load - log10(edna_load_factor))

# sample-level estimates
m0_samples = m0_df %>%
  group_by(sample, sample_type, load_obs_c) %>%
  summarise(n_wells = n(),
            n_detected = sum(detected),
            obs_sd_log10 = if_else(n_detected > 1, sd(log10(bd_load[detected])), NA_real_),
            .groups = "drop")

mu_sample = posterior_linpred(m0, newdata = m0_samples, dpar = "mu") / log(10)
sigma_sample = posterior_linpred(m0, newdata = m0_samples, dpar = "sigma", transform = TRUE) / log(10)

m0_samples = m0_samples %>%
  mutate(log10_load = apply(mu_sample, 2, median),
         sigma_log10 = apply(sigma_sample, 2, median),
         share_detected = n_detected / n_wells)

# load range supported by samples with detected wells (beyond it the curves extrapolate)
m0_data_range = m0_samples %>%
  filter(n_detected > 0) %>%
  summarise(lo = quantile(log10_load, 0.05), hi = quantile(log10_load, 0.95)) %>%
  unlist()
```

Left: well-to-well noise SD against latent load. Points are each sample's observed SD between detected wells (samples with ≥ 2 detected wells); the dashed line is Poisson sampling of copies alone. Right: per-well detection; points are each sample's share of wells detected, at its estimated latent load. Line and band: population-level curve (posterior median, 90% interval); shaded areas lie outside the middle 90% of sample loads (extrapolation). Ticks along the bottom are the experiment's positive results by qPCR lab, as copies per reaction × 40, so results line up by copies in the well (PrepMan results sit lower here than their swab load, since PrepMan extracts are diluted 80× rather than 40×).

```{r m0-curves-plot}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show curve plot code"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

experiment_positive = snarl_clean %>%
  filter(bd_load > 0, !is.na(bd_start_quant)) %>%
  mutate(log10_load = log10(edna_load_factor * bd_start_quant),
         qpcr_lab = paste(toupper(qpcr_lab), "qPCR (experiment)"))

copies_axis = sec_axis(~ . - log10(edna_load_factor), name = "log10(Bd copies per reaction)")

extrapolation = list(
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = m0_data_range[["lo.5%"]], ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1),
  annotate("rect", xmin = m0_data_range[["hi.95%"]], xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1)
)

curve_layers = function(which) {
  d = m0_curves %>% filter(curve == which)
  list(geom_ribbon(data = d, aes(log10_load, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.4, inherit.aes = FALSE),
       geom_line(data = d, aes(log10_load, med), colour = "grey20", inherit.aes = FALSE))
}

experiment_rug = geom_rug(data = experiment_positive, aes(log10_load, linetype = qpcr_lab),
                          inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.6)

p_noise = ggplot(m0_samples %>% filter(n_detected >= 2), aes(log10_load, obs_sd_log10)) +
  extrapolation +
  geom_function(fun = function(x) 0.434 / sqrt(10^x / edna_load_factor), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  curve_layers("sigma_log10") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = sample_type), alpha = 0.6) +
  experiment_rug +
  scale_x_continuous(sec.axis = copies_axis) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.8)) +
  labs(x = "latent log10(Bd load per swab), Qiagen scale", y = "well-to-well SD (log10)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

p_detect = ggplot(m0_samples, aes(log10_load, share_detected)) +
  extrapolation +
  curve_layers("p_detect") +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = sample_type), width = 0, height = 0.03, alpha = 0.6) +
  experiment_rug +
  scale_x_continuous(sec.axis = copies_axis) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 5)) +
  labs(x = "latent log10(Bd load per swab), Qiagen scale", y = "P(well detected)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

p_noise + p_detect
```

Curve values at selected loads (posterior median, 90% interval).

```{r m0-curves-table}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show curve table code"

m0_curves %>%
  filter(round(log10_load, 2) %in% c(1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4)) %>%
  mutate(value = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", med, lo, hi),
         extrapolated = log10_load < m0_data_range[["lo.5%"]] | log10_load > m0_data_range[["hi.95%"]]) %>%
  select(curve, log10_load, log10_copies, value, extrapolated) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = curve, values_from = value) %>%
  rename(`log10 load per swab` = log10_load,
         `log10 copies per reaction` = log10_copies,
         `P(detected)` = p_detect,
         `noise SD (log10)` = sigma_log10) %>%
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Posterior predictive checks

Share of wells detected, median positive log10 load, and pooled within-sample SD of log10 load among detected wells (samples with ≥ 2 detected wells), overall and by the sample's observed load.

```{r m0-ppc}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show PPC code"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

m0_yrep = posterior_predict(m0, ndraws = 500)

# pooled within-sample SD of log10 load among detected wells, optionally by a grouping of rows
pooled_within_sd = function(y, group = "all") {
  tibble(sample = m0_df$sample, group = group, y = y) %>%
    filter(y > 0) %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    filter(n() >= 2) %>%
    mutate(dev = log10(y) - mean(log10(y))) %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    summarise(sd = sqrt(sum(dev^2) / (n() - n_distinct(sample))), .groups = "drop")
}

(ppc_stat(y = m0_df$bd_load, yrep = m0_yrep, stat = function(y) mean(y > 0)) +
    labs(x = "share of wells detected")) +
  (ppc_stat(y = m0_df$bd_load, yrep = m0_yrep, stat = function(y) median(log10(y[y > 0]))) +
     labs(x = "median log10(Bd load), detected wells")) +
  (ppc_stat(y = m0_df$bd_load, yrep = m0_yrep, stat = function(y) pooled_within_sd(y)$sd) +
     labs(x = "pooled within-sample SD (log10)"))
```

```{r m0-ppc-by-load}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show PPC by load code"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5

load_bin = cut(m0_df$load_obs, c(-Inf, 2, 2.5, 3, Inf))

ppc_bins_rep = map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(m0_yrep)), ~ pooled_within_sd(m0_yrep[.x, ], load_bin)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(med = median(sd), lo = quantile(sd, 0.05), hi = quantile(sd, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ppc_bins_obs = pooled_within_sd(m0_df$bd_load, load_bin)

ggplot(ppc_bins_rep, aes(group, med)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, colour = "replicated (median, 90%)")) +
  geom_point(data = ppc_bins_obs, aes(group, sd, colour = "observed"), size = 3, shape = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("observed" = "black", "replicated (median, 90%)" = "grey50")) +
  labs(x = "observed sample load (log10 per swab)", y = "pooled within-sample SD (log10)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Shrinkage of latent loads

Each sample's estimated latent load (posterior median) against its observed mean log10 load of detected wells, by number of detected wells. Points on the 1:1 line are not shrunk. Samples with one detected well carry little information on their own load and are pulled toward the centre of the latent-load distribution (dotted line); strong upward shrinkage at low loads overpredicts the median positive load. High-load samples with several agreeing wells should stay on the line.

```{r m0-shrinkage}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show shrinkage check code"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5

m0_samples %>%
  filter(n_detected > 0) %>%
  mutate(load_obs = load_obs_c + load_center,
         n_detected = factor(n_detected)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(load_obs, log10_load, colour = n_detected)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(m0_pop$mu_0) / log(10), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "observed mean log10(Bd load), detected wells", y = "latent log10(Bd load), posterior median",
       colour = "detected wells",
       title = paste("latent intercepts:", latent_dist)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Export for Model 2

Posterior draws and summaries of population-level effects, group-level SDs, and correlations, plus the noise and detection curves (per draw and summarised) and the load range supported by data, saved to `fits/m0_qpcr_noise_export.rds`. The export is overwritten by whichever `latent_dist` was rendered last (recorded in `settings`).

```{r m0-export}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show Export code"

m0_draws = as_draws_df(m0) %>%
  subset_draws(variable = c("^b_", "^sd_", "^cor_"), regex = TRUE)

m0_summary = m0_draws %>%
  summarise_draws(mean, sd, median,
                  ~ quantile(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)))

m0_export = list(summary = m0_summary,
                 draws = m0_draws,
                 curves = m0_curves,
                 curve_draws = m0_curve_draws %>% select(draw, log10_load, p_detect, sigma_log10),
                 data_range_log10_load = m0_data_range,
                 load_factor = edna_load_factor,
                 load_center = load_center,
                 settings = list(include_tissue = include_tissue, include_all_zero = include_all_zero,
                                 latent_dist = latent_dist,
                                 student_df = if (latent_dist == "student") student_df else NA),
                 formula = m0_formula,
                 import_date = edna_import_date,
                 export_date = Sys.Date())

saveRDS(m0_export, here(fit_dir, "m0_qpcr_noise_export.rds"))

m0_summary %>%
  kable(digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```
